ResponsesInList.Title: TinyMCE Editor scrolls to top when clicking margin areas in Chrome (Moodle 4.5.6+)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone, We’ve run into a strange behavior with the TinyMCE editor in Moodle 4.5.6+. When editing text, if you click in the margin area of elements (for example around images, tables, or other block elements), the mouse cursor changes to a pointer. If you click there, the page suddenly scrolls back to the very top of the editor/document. This only happens in Chrome (latest stable version). In Firefox , the same action does not trigger any scroll. Worth mentioning: we have custom stylesheets injected into the editor’s iframe , so it might be related to that. It’s quite disruptive when working on long texts, since you lose your place every time this happens. Steps to see the problem: Open any TinyMCE editor in Moodle. Insert a block element (e.g. ul or image or table). Hover near the element’s margin until the cursor turns into a pointer. Click. The editor jumps to the top. Has anyone else noticed this? Is it a known Chrome/TinyMCE issue, or something specific to Moodle’s integration? Thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: TinyMCE Editor scrolls to top when clicking margin areas in Chrome (Moodle 4.5.6+)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I’ve solved the issue! The root cause was an injected CSS rule that modified the body height of the iframe: html, body { height: 100%; } This CSS alone is enough to break the normal behavior.

ResponsesInList.Title: Settings for "Fallback" in TinyMCE multilang
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I cannot find any settings to specify "Fallback" language in the TinyMC multilang tool. I'd prefer to have the option removed from the menu, or if that's not possible set Swedish as fallback language. Now it just says "Other"

ResponsesInList.Title: Settings for "Fallback" in TinyMCE multilang
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, The fallback in the multilang filter does not specify any language in particular. In your case, you may use the english and other language tags, or use english and swedish (meaning the same). If you would add french to your site: * in case of english and other, the content in other would also appear when the user has french selected. * in case of english and swedish, the user would not see the content between these language tags, because french is not present. AFAIK the other fallback works only if the language content is within the same paragraph. Best regards, Stephan

ResponsesInList.Title: Settings for "Fallback" in TinyMCE multilang
ResponsesInList.Text: I understand, Stephan. But would prefer to not have the option at all. We use the multilang v2 filter and our users will only be confused by the option. On the plugin info page it seem as if deactivating Fallback in the menu was possible, it says " If you don't use the multilang2 filter , check that the setting `fallbackspantag` is active". But I cannot find any setting for it. https://moodle.org/plugins/tiny_multilang2

ResponsesInList.Title: Settings for "Fallback" in TinyMCE multilang
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, in the main branch of the repo (not yet officially release) I have added a setting to disable the "fallback (other)" option. The setting `fallbackspantag` has been removed in version 1.1. This setting was to control whether to use the Moodle standard span tags when the multilang2 filter is installed. Now this is automatically checked, the mulitlang2 annotation is preferred over the Moodle standard annotation but this tiny plugin can handle both, so you may use it to create multi language content even without having the multilang2 filter installed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Settings for "Fallback" in TinyMCE multilang
ResponsesInList.Text: Excellent, thank you very much, Stephan!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: TinyMCE customizing the toolbar
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, Apologies for the delay in getting back to you all on this - I had hoped to do so earlier. With TinyMCE 6 we deliberately chose not to implement an admin configuration similar to the configuration we had for Atto. There are a few reasons behind that but the main reasons are that it is significantly harder to do so with TinyMCE than Atto, we want to encourage developers to consider their own inclusion themselves, and we also have paved the way for those needing to to create their own TinyMCE plugins to configure the editor from within a plugin itself. When it comes to the difficulty this is partially because TinyMCE has both toolbar buttons, and also Menus. With the combination of the two it becomes much more complex to create a meaningful, complete, and bug-free interface to configure from Moodle. With regards the final point about paving the way for plugins managing config, one request we have had quite a bit is to allow different TinyMCE plugin configurations for different editor usages, or user types, or similar. This is something I've wanted to include for some time but with Atto it was extremely difficult, especially given the user interface for managing plugins. To solve this we have designed our TinyMCE architecture that a developer can create a configuration plugin which reconfigures the menus, toolbars, and other configuration. This could be to make specific changes (for example adding, or removing items), or it could be to make more elaborate changes such as changing configuration for specific users, or specific users of the editor (for example, a quiz question in edit mode). I know that this approach was appealing to a number of user groups I've spoken with. Hope this helps, Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: TinyMCE - Selecting a colour palate
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Justin, We've disabled this in the core Moodle product for a number of reasons and you should be aware of these before re-enabling them. Firstly the issue you touch upon, accessibity. Colour is often, incorrectly, used to convey meaning. The old 'Green means good, red means bad'. That may be fine for a lot of users, but it's a problem for many. In the example syou give (key concepts, case studies, reflection, deadlines, warnings)... these are all conveying an important concept and colour alone should not be used for this. The other main issue is that of fitting in with themes. Again, you touch on this, but the problem is more involved. Whilst you can probably find a set of colours which fit with your current theme with _relative_ ease, TinyMCE stores colours as hex in style attributes on the element itself. Should your organisation ever change their theme, their colour palette, or even just allow users to select a different theme (e.g. for accessibility resaons), the colours will nto change and cannot be easily changed in line with the theme without modifying the content further.

ResponsesInList.Title: What stopps sites switching to TinyMCE as default
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, In a german forum of Moodle in higher education we recently a thread with the question about the experiences from moving to TinyMCE as the default editor. What keeps sites away from moving to Tiny at the moment? One note beforehand, in recent Moodle versions fixes and improvments were done in the TinyMCE intregration. Not all of the issues mentioned below are from Moodle 4.3. Some of the things might be resolved already in the current 4.4 release. I will here try to list various aspects and obstacles that were mentioned when the TinyMCE was in use. I just comment here without having this verified. Some of the reports are also a bit unspecific. Missing broader formatting options (other font sizes etc...) For the worst case we recommend switch back to Atto or even use plain text. Also what is considerable from my experience: technical departments such as math, physics, chemistry, computer sciense tend to use more technical annotations (Tex, source code, chemistry formulas) that cause problems when edited with the TinyMCE. This is a filter that lists issues in the TinyMCE component that are open or in development: https://tracker.moodle.org/issues/?filter=25025 For all that are afrait of loosing functionality: If something is not working as excpected please check, who is involved (teachers only or all users). When teachers only, how big is the group? Is there a chance to provide them with a feasible workaround? In our institution the computer sience department faces the most problems but these people are also the most skilled ones. HTH in the development and in migration stategies. Stephan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: TinyMCE images_reuse_filename

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: TinyMCE 6 in Moodle 4.1.4
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Joost, Is there a setting we can manipulate to get autosave to work with TinyMCE 6? I went about writing some text in a mod_page that was previously saved, then quit the page using the cancel button, and returned afterwards: my last additions weren't saved, so the expected autosave version of the page wasn't restored. You'd expect a warning 'Leaving this page without saving', and a notice 'A previous version of this text has been restored'. This does work out of the box and there is no configuration required. The autosave will push changes every time TinyMCE create an undo point - that's typically whenever you press the [return] key, change focus, etc. The issue here is that by pressing the "Cancel" button you are clearing the form content and resetting all state. When that happens we deliberately clear the autosave content as we've done for many years with our previous editors. If you just refresh the page, then you will get both the form change detetion, and the editor autosave. We have no idea what this plugin actually does, so we checked the TinyMCE documentation on what we thought was the same plugin. What does this plugin do? Does it handle all the Moodle filter features? Or something else. In any case, documentation on this seems to be missing. This is a Moodle plugin, not the native TinyMCE plugin. It is purely used to create a link to either an external website, a Moodle page, or some content, within your text. It integrates with the Moodle repository plugin to allow you to search for, and insert, some Moodle-specific content. It also provides you with an interface to configure some additional options such as setting the link text (instead of using the URL ), and opening the link in a new window. Regarding the accessibility questions: Images with empty or no ALT text --> We found that images with alt="" are skipped, but images without the alt="" and/or role="presentation" do get noticed. This is a valid case and the documented approach for decorative images per the W3C Accessibility Initiative , who specifically note: In these cases, a null (empty) alt text should be provided (alt="") so that they can be ignored by assistive technologies, such as screen readers. Text values for these types of images would add audible clutter to screen reader output or could distract users if the topic is different from that in adjacent text. Leaving out the alt attribute is also not an option because when it is not provided, some screen readers will announce the file name of the image instead. This is therefore a correct behaviour. Long text without proper headings gets noticed, but as soon as you'd add a few headers at the bottom of this, the 'long text, please break up with headings' notice disappears. I'm sure we can improve this detection. I'd suggest raising an issue in the Moodle Tracker to improve this. Table issues don't get reported, at least not the way I built one: A table created in TinyMCE doesn't get reported (instead it breaks the entire report even if there are issues elsewhere in the text). If you're able to, please raise an issue in the Moodle tracker with an example content that breaks for you and/or replication instructions. Then I added an MS Word created table (3 rows, 4 columns, no data, no captions or column headers, 2 cells merged), and got a whole bunch of information. The Moodle Docs may need clarification on 'tables created with applications such as MS Word or similar'. Unfortunately content from applications like Word is typically full of rubbish content which is very hard to clear. We are constantly trying to improve this. Text contrast issues work as expected, but then one expects a user to mess up the text in an application such as MS Word (or know HTML), since text color isn't an option (yet) in Tiny 6. I'm not sure I understand this question? Best wishes, Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: TinyMCE key event logger plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi! I'm actively developing a plugin for Moodle using TinyMCE which captures key event data. Our first release has been submitted to the plugin repository: https://moodle.org/plugins/tiny_keylogger (pending review as of 5/24/23 with an estimated 130-day wait). The plugin captures and formats the data into a downloadable JSON file format available to editing teachers and the administrator with the right URL . The files are structured, user ID obfuscated, UNIX time-stamped streams from the writing process. The file format is compatible with a separate service we've created, so far with this data we have created ML which can verify the authorship of a single student across time (e.g. we can verify that the student remains the author accessing the online text area over time and across submissions) calculating the time and effort of the writing process, calculate editing %, character counts, writing efficiency estimate the amount of text that was entered via copy/paste provide guidance on the amount of text injected via AI extension (such as Grammarly and Google's autocomplete While the calculations are offline currently, we're developing this service further to connect the ML via API. If you're interested in learning more while we wait for the plugin review, let me know (code is also posted here: https://github.com/cursiveinc/moodle-tinymce_keylogger -Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: [4.1.0] TinyMCE core version: color picker
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Andreas, Thanks for your feedback. At the moment this is not possible and we are looking at doing so in MDL-76517 . TinyMCE does include a colour plugin as standard which we have disabled as it is not compatible with either accessible content creation or our theme infrastructure. We are trying to work out how best to solve this combination, likely offering a small subset of colours which themes can define and control. As it stands, if content is written using the standard TinyMCE colour plugin and the theme supports a Dark mode (for example), then it is highly likely that you'll see contrast issues with the content. We want to prevent that before it becomes a difficult problem to solve.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Issues with the TinyMCE editor stripping a tag that is used by my filter
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Andrew, It looks like there are two things going on. Firstly, TinyMCE removes empty tags - you can see that by putting the tag in place, and toggling the HTML view off and on - it completely removes it. If you put some content in it, then it will be wrapped in a

tag instead. If you put some content in the tag, for example: ```text   ``` When it is saved I _suspect_ that the `data-id` is removed from the form by `trusttext_pre_edit()`, or `clean_text()` which call HTMLPurifier. HTML Purifier automatically removes all unknown tags. At present I believe we do not provide a way to have customised HTML Purifier configuration so to support this we'd have to look at how best to do so. For a local hack you could add: ```text if ($def = $config->maybeGetRawHTMLDefinition()) { $def->addAttribute('span', 'data-translationhash', 'CDATA'); } ``` Note: You may need to clear the cache for this to take effect, or temporarily add: ```text $config->set(' Cache .DefinitionImpl', null); // TODO: remove this later! ``` Hope this helps, Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: رد: how to copy paste coloured text from microsoft word
ResponsesInList.Text: In MS Word, the formatting of every paragraph and other attributes of that paragraph are at the end of the paragraph. Highlight the end of the paragraph and you'll see what looks to be something that's longer than a space.   Hidden.   Invisible and is really machine language. Color attributes enclose the text. IF you had php-tidy installed, that supposedly helps those that wanna copy and paste from Word ... uhhhh, not recommended, really cause one is coping Microsoft's html tagging which ballons what might have been 1K into the 20'sK ... tags for every friggin' line! :| Rendering in Moodle won't be exactly like you see it in Word and attempting to use html source to fix in Moodle, not worth the effort ( IMHO ). But ... you could copy and paste from Word to NotePad the text ... that strips out M$ junk ... paste into Moodle from NotePad. Color however won't come into it. Best to use color in the Moodle editor ... reduces M$ Junk tagging. Yes, am a M$ hater ... and proud of it! My 2 cents! 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Copy-paste images are not visible to students
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I've found some strange behaviour in Moodle, I wondered if the community had any thoughts. Suppose I create a Page in Moodle, and add two images to it. For the first image, I open the image in Preview (or equivalent Windows application), copy it to clipboard, then paste it into the text editor (Atto or TinyMCE, same results on each). Next, I add the image again in the proper way - I click the image button, select the file, upload , add alt-text and save. I then save the page and it looks like this: Now, I log in as a different user, a student in my course. I return to the page, and this is what I see: The pasted image is not visible to the student. Now I know I am not supposed to copy-paste images into the text editor. But our users on the whole do not, and of course they do paste images in, as it is the most obvious easy way to add them. And because the image shows up fine to the editor, they do not know that there is a problem - but their students never see the image. Looking at the code, I can see that the pasted image is stored in the HTML as a Base-64 encoded string of data. That code remains intact in the HTML after saving the Page, but Moodle is stripping it out when it renders the Page to the student. Does anyone have any insights into this? For example, any answers to the questions: Why does Atto/TinyMCE allow the pasting of images at all, when it will not work? Why doesn't Moodle at least strip out the image for the editor, so they can see that there is a problem? Is there anything we can do, other than user training, to stop this happening? PS I see on Tracker that pasting will be properly supported in 3.9, which is great. So hopefully this is a temporary problem. Thanks all Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Atto performance issues (lock-ups) in Safari in Moodle 3.8, 3.9
ResponsesInList.Text: We recently upgraded to Moodle 3.8, and we're seeing some rather major performance issues with the Atto editor when using the Safari browser, and also to a lesser extent on Chrome (MacOS). We also see this on 3.9 (using sandbox.moodledemo.net). We’re not seeing any problems on Firefox (MacOS). We don’t see this in Windows... mainly Safari and Chrome on the Mac. What we're seeing is unresponsiveness and lock-ups in Atto when using Safari. For example, when writing on a page, selecting some text, the selecting the Heading toolbar icon, we see a stutter in how Atto reacts. Oftentimes, one has to wait a second or two for the change to take place. This sluggishness seems to be especially prevalent when using the Font Color toolbar, or any Atto toolbar plug-in with a menu. Selecting text, then selecting a color, one usually has to wait a couple seconds for the change to take place. And then, you usually can't do anything in the browser for a couple seconds or more, until it unfreezes and returns you control. UCLA has confirmed that this issue exists on their Moodle 3.9 site. I’m wondering if anyone else has encountered this. We created a Moodle Tracker issue for this ( https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-69292 ). We actually determined what was causing the problem and developed a fix. We have implemented it on our site... it works fine. We’re hoping to get more up-votes on the tracker issue so this can be addressed in Moodle core. Thanks... Brian

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Use wwwroot variable in ATTO
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle will use wwwroot variable for all internal links thus rather than using a url to images when developing on a localhost, upload the images to the localhost moodle via moodle. When a backup of the course is made to restore to your production server , images should be included in the backup. Please see: https://docs.moodle.org/38/en/Images 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Use wwwroot variable in ATTO
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Matheus, The short answer is no , and we will not accept any change which introduces such a 'feature'. The wwwroot variable is used to ensure that there is one, authoritative, URL for the site. Moodle has a number of places which expect that you are accessing it via the correct address. If you are not then you will likely enter a number of weird issues such as this one. Additionally you'll see that if you don't use the correct address the files you have uploaded will be removed after approximately 4 days because they will not have been picked up by the file processor when parsing the text, and they will therefore not be moved from the draft files area. If you really want to use the internal IP address, then I suggest you set the IP in your local host file. Something like https://www.howtogeek.com/howto/27350/beginner-geek-how-to-edit-your-hosts-file/ will help you find out how to do so. Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Use wwwroot variable in ATTO
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, When you move your site (change it's URL ), you have to change all URLs from the old site to the new one. Hopefully, Moodle provides a tool for that : Search and replace tool . HTH , Séverin

ResponsesInList.Title: Ordered vs. Unordered List Formatting Discrepancy
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there, An instructor at our institution reported a strange formatting discrepancy in ATTO between bullet and numbered lists, namely that the numbered ones are indented and the bullet ones are not. Certainly not the biggest deal but certainly an annoyance for users who want to enter text in the system in a particular way. Digging around, we found this is due to some css overriding the indent on the ul elements and have verified that this occurs in the base boost theme the moodle demo site in the latest version (see attached screenshot). I'm wondering if this is something anyone else has run into and tried to overcome? Or if there is an existing tracker item I could through a vote onto to get this fixed upstream? Regards, Dave

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ordered vs. Unordered List Formatting Discrepancy
ResponsesInList.Text:
I can report the exact same indentation bug in Moodle 3.5.2.
So far I haven't found any better solution than setting an inline left margin for the list. For example: 
```text
<ul style="margin-left: 2rem;">
```
 Hope this gets solved in future versions of Moodle. Cheers!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ordered vs. Unordered List Formatting Discrepancy
ResponsesInList.Text: Quick update: I've tested this on a few different browsers and noticed that the bullets are not indented properly only in Google Chrome. Please check the below image: You'll notice some other differences in the way different browsers display the list, e.g. the margin between bullet and text, the size of the bullet itself, the overall font size... So you only need to manually indent the bullets if the majority of your users are working with Chrome. If multiple browsers are used throughout the organization, I'd suggest double-checking any style customization in all of them, just in case. This isn't the first time I've found Chrome annoying for styling Moodle courses. It keeps doing awkward stuff like adding random spans with inline styles concerning font-size, line-height etc... It just has its own opinion about how pages should be displayed and that's that

ResponsesInList.Title: Customising Atto toolbar in a form editor
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi, I'm writing a plugin which includes a form with an Atto editor, but I don't want the standard buttons defined in the editor_atto | toolbar setting. I have come up with a way to do this but it needs a core patch, so would like a sanity check in case there's an easier way to do it. In the form definition: 
```text
        $editor_toolbar = <<<EOT


collapse = collapse


style1 = title, bold, italic


list = unorderedlist, orderedlist


indent = indent
```
 The patch just passes the atto:toolbar string from the form definition when constructing the MoodleQuickForm_editor: 
```text
--- a/lib/form/editor.php


+++ b/lib/form/editor.php


@@ -99,6 +99,11 @@ class MoodleQuickForm_editor extends HTML_QuickForm_element implements templatab


         // Note: for some reason the code using this setting does not like bools.


         $this->_options['subdirs'] = (int)($this->_options['subdirs'] == 1);


 


+        // Atto toolbar options.


+        if (!empty($options['atto:toolbar'])) {


+            $this->_options['atto:toolbar'] = $options['atto:toolbar'];


+        }


+


         editors_head_setup();
```
 If there's a way to do it without the patch - I'd love to hear it! If not, I can create an issue in the tracker. Cheers, Dave.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Customising Atto toolbar in a form editor
ResponsesInList.Text: I've created MDL-64512 for this.

ResponsesInList.Title: Best practise (assessability) for use with TinyMCE
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I have been asked to enable the TinyMCE editor for our Moodle site. I think the editor is great and really powerful for my teacher's. However i am a bit concerned as to the use of new background colours, and their application within courses as my Teachers are not technical, therefore their understanding of design, UX and accessibility is very low. I know there is an accessibility checker (perfect!) but i don't want to end up with courses pink text on red background any ideas? Kind Regards, Leticia

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best practise (assessability) for use with TinyMCE
ResponsesInList.Text: That is an issue, even for experienced writers occasionally. Best bet is to educate your teachers. Show them what you do not want them to do. 1. Create a presentation that has examples of what you do not want to see 2. Convert the presentation to a video, e.g new versions of PowerPoint can convert presentations to a wmv file. 3. If needed Convert wmv file to mp4 and put it into the Moodle - Handbrake will easily convert most formats. 5. Make your presentation at a staff meeting, so everyone gets the message, and your mp4 file is uploaded to a Staff only course on what to do, how to use the new editor. 6. Trust your teachers to mostly get it right, and those few who get it wrong, well, they can be reeducated but it can take a few tries. Colour is always an issue, so talk about the colour wheel, and talk about opposites offering high contrast, which is what text should always be. Too  much colour overwhelms the message Too little colour makes it boring and detracts from the message So the message is keep colours to a minimum, but keep them simple. One issue that is a lot more common than we think is background colour. If background colour is too light there is a risk of luminosity overwhelming the text and the message is lost. Some younger people are subject to serious problems with Irlen's Syndrome where luminosity is preventing them of following the text. They need a muted pastel colour, a blue often works, but a pastel green can be ok too, with very dark text, black on green or navy on pastel blue, not red on green. In Oz, it is an unsettling truth that many Aboriginals have Irlen's and it is rarely diagnosed adequately. It is actually even more common amongst Middle Eastern peoples I have been told. Is also not that uncommon in European and Asian populations either. It is similar to dyslexia, but can have a much deeper impact and the two are often confused. Colour blindness too is an issue, so red on green and green on red should always be avoided. Be careful of the "signal colours". Red, yellow and green. Reds and yellows are warning colours, so should really be avoided, muted or pastel greens can be useful in large blocks, are are better used for highlighting a line of text to draw attention to it: Greens can be used to attract attention to important notes but green text needs to be bold otherwise it is lost on this background. Brick colour, not red, can also be used to attract attention to a critical point. Again, it has to be in bold to avoid being overwhelmed by the luminosity of the background. Try these things in a word processing document, see what works what doesn't then use that to build your presentation. Good luck

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best practise (assessability) for use with TinyMCE
ResponsesInList.Text: While you might find a way to prevent ... why not appeal to teachers understanding that color does affect learning and as educators they should 'sacrifice' their preferences for colors and consider the students. https://elearningindustry.com/4-tips-use-color-in-elearning Is but one reference ... one could probably find some 'brain research' addressing color on the net somewhere as well. Got a training course for your teachers?   Create a course for them to take and choose, on purpose, the most awfull color cominbations you can imagine ... ie, make it hard to read and distracts. 2 cent opinion ... True story  ... I once worked in summers painting classrooms.  The supervisor of the painting crews dropped off appropriate latex for walls and semi-gloss for trim + a direction to paint room #.  Room # was on the East side of the building ... morning sun ... and the building itself was constructed in the 1920's ... classroom on second floor and had very tall bay windows which required painters to use a ladder to paint the walls/window trim on that side of the classroom. Teacher in that room had been very critical of many things on the campus including things like facilities, AC (of which there was none - Texas), drab color of classrooms, etc. The color we were to use (had to use) ... lime green.  My painting partner and I both asked the supervisor if he was sure!!!   Supervisor who was to retired at the close of summer smiled and said 'Yep!' I didn't teach on that campus, but heard from other teachers I knew on that campus how much trouble the teacher in Room # had that year with discipline of students. Go figure! :\ 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: HTML Snippets Plugin

It works a bit like Generico. It is much simpler. The html is simply generated when the user presses the insert button. I hope to release it one day on the Moodle plugins database . But for now its just available for anyone to use from Github. https://github.com/justinhunt/moodle-atto_snippet

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HTML Snippets Plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Generally, over my years of using Moodle, whenever I wanted to set up a Moodle page to have a particular look or layout using any of the Moodle editors, I have done it by using tables with various rows and columns with some cells merged to get the look I want. It was always a pain in the backside. However, using tables this way in snippets makes this VERY easy to do. BUT, if you do any research, it is NOT recommended to use tables for layout like that as it make for some pretty complicated HTML. Instead, it is recommended to use all the new HTML5 stuff, such as flexboxes,etc. Unfortunately, I've discovered that the style  stuff that makes the HTML5 look right, gets ignored when used in a snippet as soon as you save the page you are creating. I've discovered four options. One - the style info has to be placed in the Custom CSS of the theme you are using. If you are like me, and let people pick the theme to use, then to keep things from breaking, the style info has to be added to EVERY theme. Not a good option as in my case, I currently have 20 themes installed. Option Two - Snippet does contain a styles.css file. If the style info is placed there, then purge all caches, the styling takes effect in every theme. Also not really a good option as any page created with a snippet will break as soon as/if you upgrade the Snippet plugin. Option three and four - Generico Filter templates and PoodLL Filter Widget templates both have a Custom CSS field setting that when used, makes the styles show up in any theme used. This makes all the new HTML5 stuff usable/doable. Sooooo - I guess the point of this rambling discourse is - can you think of any way to make the CSS style stuff work in a Snippet? Is it possible to add a Custom CSS field to each snippet or, probably better, as an optional spot on the Snippet settings page?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HTML Snippets Plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: About adding a CSS styles area to each snippet, I think its not the best idea. The main reason is that the functionality needed to make that work, takes us into Generico land. If it can't be done in snippet, its better done in Generico. ( I am growing uneasy that we have invented a new language here ..) But you can apply CSS classes that have been declared elsewhere, eg to turn links into bootstrap buttons. So I think its just better that the CSS classes are declared in the theme or theme's custom CSS area, and they are used in the snippet. It makes sharing snippets like that across sites, a bit tedious. My comment earlier about loading presets from the theme, is related to this. Because it means theme designers could ship templates that work with the CSS from the theme, with their theme.

```text
this.addButton({
```

```text
$iconmap['
```

```text
this.addBasicButton({


      exec: 'removeFormat',

```

```text
core:
e/clear_formatting
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ATTO wordimport table extraction failure
ResponsesInList.Text: In general, the plugin does not retain the styling of table cells or borders, although it does retain formatting such as merged row and column cells, and heading and body rows. The rationale is that it is preferable for the table to conform to the styling conventions defined for the Moodle site. For example, I use the following CSS definitions to set the look of tables to have heading rows with white text on a blue background, every 2nd body row shaded, and borders on all cells. table { margin-bottom:1.5em;box-shadow:0.8em 0.8em 0.8em 0.4em #888;table-layout:fixed} table, td, th { border:1px solid blue} tr { vertical-align:top;} thead tr { background-color:blue;color:white;} tbody > tr:nth-child(2n+1) {background-color:gray} This requires that you have access to the theme design pages, and that the design permits the inclusion of custom CSS. I believe that modern themes support this (e.g. Essential, Adaptable).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ATTO editor loses code changes on save
ResponsesInList.Text: Richard, this is not simple.  The simplest Fail case is if you have a little bit of code (and at present the only code I have used is for Tabs) then if you paste into the editor any unformatted text (for instance a web link) the editor then deletes all the code that makes the tabs work. I'd be interested if you could explain exactly what is happening for you. One of the threads on this is here: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=347847 Another: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=347860 Tracker item is here: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-58084 Ryan Wylie has posted in the tracker thread saying this is not a bug: Unfortunately this doesn't appear to be a bug with atto from what I can tell. As Mark mentioned above, if you're using the WYSIWYG view on the atto editor the code behind the scenes will attempt to sanitise a few things in the content that you're pasting in an attempt to keep consistent styling (depending on where you are copying the content from, it can come along with a lot more information than what you see in the page). The WYSISYG editor isn't really suitable to generate rich HTML widgets (though you can sometimes get it to work), such as tabs, because it is very easy to generate invalid HTML (especially when pasting content from different sources). It's quite a bit more complex to write a full widget than to mark up some simple content. If you have a need to build something a little more complex then it's best to do it in the code view within atto (click the "show/hide advanced buttons" -> HTML button). This will allow you to write the HTML directly, though it does require a bit more of an advanced knowledge of HTML I'm afraid. I'd like the Atto settings to be adjusted so that the cleanup/sanitising is a little less aggressive, but from what Ryan says, this is not likely to happen.  He has suggested using the html view to code what he calls widgets (like a few tabs); this is too much like hard work for me. Possible fix/kludge work around Mark Sharp posted this, which introduces the idea of pasting from M$Word, which may hep you: So, when you paste into atto, it is expecting some kind of formatting to come along with it. e.g. Pasting from Word or from a website. It identifies it as such and does some clean up, then pastes your text from the clipboard. And, actually that works. If you paste from a website, you don't lose all your formatting. However, if you try to be clean and paste from a text editor, the clipboard doesn't having any formatting information, so atto runs a function called fallbackPasteCleanup (you can see this in your browser console if you have the dev tools open - usually F12 opens that). This cleanup seems to be a little more rigourous and applies this._cleanPasteHTML to all the content rather than just the pasted content. You can see the problem with this: you will being a lot of odd formatting from your source web page or word document, and this makes your HTML look a mess. In the last version I used (Moodle Verson 3.0) the cut and paste from Notepad process was flawless, so this new behaviour has come in in version 3.1 or 3.2. Just in case you missed my request: I'd be interested in exactly what is happening for you. Good luck -Derek

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Removing/stripping of code
ResponsesInList.Text: There are actually several good reasons WHY editors or core moodle strip tags. Editors have validation rules that check source and iframe & script-tags are under special control in core tinymce javascript file. If you need to add iframe-tags you can disable editor from your user profile. Pressing <> in editor does not prevent validation - editor just switches to "html-mode". If some "normal" html tags get stripped there is usually something wrong in source - some attributes may not be valid or some tags are used in a wrong way.

Atto is based on HTML5 content-editable http://www.w3.org/TR/html5/editing.html#contenteditable . Some browsers (e.g. Chrome) try harder to keep the style of what you pasted similar to what you copied. That tends to lead to lots of mess like the above in the HTML. Other browser (e.g Firefox ) seem to give cleaner HTML, but that means styles are less likely to be preserved.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to change default Target in the TinyMCE 'Insert/Edit Link' dialog box?
ResponsesInList.Text: Colin is right, there is no setting for this change but you need to edit file lib/editor/tinymce/tiny_mce/ version of tinymce /plugins/advlink/js/advlink.js and there move line html += '<option value="_blank">' + tinyMCEPopup.getLang('advlink_dlg.target_blank') + ' (_blank)</option>'; before line html += '<option value="_self">' + tinyMCEPopup.getLang('advlink_dlg.target_same') + '</option>'; Save the file and test. If the change does not have effect immediately purge all caches (Site administration > Development > Purge all caches) If you have not edited files of moodle before take a copy of that file first so that if something goes wrong in editing you have the original file available...

ResponsesInList.Title: Atto Editor Word import plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: I recently released a new Atto editor plugin which allows you import Word content into any textbox in Moodle, see https://moodle.org/plugins/view/atto_wordimport . It delivers much better results than copying and pasting Word content into text fields. The main features are as follows. It imports quite clean XHTML without all the crud usually associated with pasting content from Word. It imports any images embedded in the Word file (as long as they are Internet-compatible, i.e. GIF/PNG/JPEG, but not BMP or EPS). It converts Microsoft Equation Editor equations into MathML and imports the MathML in a way that is compatible with MathJax. It imports tables, retaining merged rows and cells, but not table borders (at present). It imports the Word heading styles (Heading 1, Heading 2, etc.) into XHTML heading elements (e.g. h3, h4), and allows you specify a mapping between the heading style and the preferred element. It's just an initial release, and so may not be suitable for production servers, but it is based on a much more mature plugin ( WordTable , for importing quiz questions from Word), so I think it is worth a look nonetheless. Any feedback appreciated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Atto Editor Word import plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: The plugin ignores specific formatting such as font sizes and colours. It only maps predefined Word style names to HTML element names, for example the "List Bullet" style is converted to the li element. Well-structured and styled Word documents convert quite well into HTML, but documents with a lot of font-size changes, colours, etc. don't convert so well, although at least the result is quite clean HTML, but probably not what you had hoped for. A workaround for this issue would be to define named styles in Word to represent the specific formatting you would like, so if you want bold red text, define a character style called "BoldRed". The conversion process should convert this to something like text. You can then create a CSS style in your theme to make the text appear how you want: ".BoldRed { font-weight: bold; color: red}".

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: problems with links to mp4 files
ResponsesInList.Text: Luis, I think we are getting a little closer. As Rick notes, spaces in URLs and file names are a bit unreliable. Try to name any files or directories you use without using spaces. That may not be the problem however. Draft files are temporary files that are only really accessible by a particular user. They only really exist when you are editing a particular text area. When the text area is saved, the file becomes a nice permanent one, and the temporary file will be deleted. A permanent file's url likely includes "pluginfile.php," but certainly won't include draftfile.php. The url that you are linking to is a draft file url. So it is wrong. It will only work under certain conditions, and this situation is not one of them. So you need to get the actual URL of the mp4 file, as it appears after the host text area has been saved. Thats the first problem. The second problem is that Moodle is clever about how it serves up files. If the mp4 files are part of a course or site that the user does not have access to (eg because they are not logged into the site that hosts the file), Moodle won't return the file. So the question then comes, where are those mp4 files actually hosted. If they are on a page in ABC course, does the user who accesses your page have access to that page in ABC course? Finally the url that you are linking to contains an ip address in place of a domain name. If that ip address is only available within your university's network, but not outside it, then your files will also be inaccessible. As complicated as that all sounds, the solution is very easy. Don't link to files in this way unless you really have some need to. Download those files, and then upload them into the text area for your quiz using the Moodle media icon on the text editor. Then if the page is accessible, so too will be the files. And you need not worry about clutter and space, 500kb is nothing, and Moodle will only store the same file once even if you use it in different places. (it's pretty clever like that.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Text in Section Summary Description block is stuck in bold format
ResponsesInList.Text: The easiest way to consider it Geoff, is that the sections are no more than Moodle's way of organising the content of the page - but that the html and css is applied across an entire page as with any standard webpage, whether its part of a cms/lms/vle or a straight forward webpage. All the browser actually sees is the final 'published' html/css (and javascript ), whether that comes from the theme, the blocks and plugins, or the user created content. The browser doesn't see Moodle's organisation of content into topic or weekly sections or its blocks and plugins, just the webpage in its entirety. So, we do get issues sometimes when a theme designer, or a user, forgets to close a div or a strong, or something similar - or where copying and pasting content from MSWord into a content area affects the whole page, not just that content area. You wont have been the first to ask similar questions and I'm sure you will be far from the last, I'm just happy it was an easy one to resolve for you

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: "A draft version of this text was automatically restored" Huh?
ResponsesInList.Text: The autosave is a feature of Atto that I believe was added in 2.8. It saves a draft copy based on context after the interval defined in the settings. If the browser window is closed prematurely, this copy is reloaded in the next page the user opens with the same context.  If the page is saved or cancelled with a button at the page bottom, the draft copies for that context are deleted so that there is a blank editor the next time. I have not notice the problem with editing questions, but I suspect that it is because the user  instead of saving is using the button "Save and continue editing" then checks the preview, and closes the window instead of saving the question again. This may also be a new feature. I just noticed it recently. You might encourage the save with the other button. Otherwise, a unwanted draft file can be removed from the editor with ctl-z or the undo button.

Click save and Ctl W to close old tab. This "short cut" would avoid some navigation, but technically Atto would probably be doing the right thing in reloading the draft. You probably may need to ask you client exactly what he is doing to figure this out.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What does "Screenreader helper" actually do?
ResponsesInList.Text: Screen readers bascially treat a content editable region like a textbox - which is wrong, because it can contain images, links and more. So the screen reader helper provides additional information about the currently selected text (e.g. is it bold), as well as a listing of any images or links in the text.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What does "Screenreader helper" actually do?
ResponsesInList.Text: Just to add, here's a slide from my last Moodle Prof Dev regarding Atto's Accessibility Checker and Screen Reader Helper. Below is an image of a text box with two different messages below it. The messages are pop ups that appear when you press the Screen Reader Helper button. Basically, it will show you if you have provided a description for the images in the text box or not. The first message displays what the reader would read out if a description is provided ("This is a description") The second message had no description provided, so according to this button, a screen reader would read the file path as the description (http://school...) As for the other button, you'll get a notice regarding color choices for people with visual impairments.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: No option to re-size with Atto and 2.7+
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi all, This is a response to this entire thread rather than a single comment within it. When we wrote the Atto editor, it was intended to be a small and simple replacement with fewer
options offered and prompts to encourage the creation of accessible content for users. Indeed, the name
`Atto` was based upon the scientific unit of measurement \( 10^{-18} \) (0.000000000000000001) - i.e.
really small. As part of this, it was decided to remove a number of buttons and options which either offer little
value, or lead to the creation of inaccessible content. In particular, we opted not to create plugins for text size, and for font colour in Atto. Both of
these plugins have historically existed in TinyMCE. When we talk about the lack of accessibility in the created content, we are not referring solely
to things like the use of clashing colours in content - that's to say a red background with green
font; or a white background with grey font. It goes much deeper than that. Often those features are
used to emphasise content within the body - highlighting an important part of the content by making
it's background colour yellow for example, or by increasing it's font size. While both of these methods will indeed highlight the content to sighted users who can clearly
see the difference between the highlighted and non-highlighted content, there is no distinction to
many other users. The most obvious examples are partially sighted, and non-sighted users who are
using screen readers. Since screen readers do not read out things like the background colour and
font size, this emphasis is entirely lost and the content is less accessible to those users. Other
affected users can include those with dyslexia and ADHD (where many sufferers will use coloured
filters to reduce the effect of certain colours and where existing colours in that content could
potentially effect the use of those filters); and colour blind users, where sufferers may be unable
to distinguish between certain colours, unable to see the effect of certain colours, or only see in
greyscale. Again, in these cases the benefit of these colour-based emphasise is either entirely
lost, or potentially leads to reduced access to the content. It's also worth bearing in mind that some of these affected conditions involve a large
cross-section of people, and that these conditions may not always be immediately apparent. Some
users may not even known themselves. Colour blindness can affect 7-10%
of men and I would guess that you're unlikely to know which of your students may be colour blind
and how your content will affect them.
Dyslexia is estimated to affects a similar number of people - the Australian Dyslexic Association estimates that 10% of the
Australian population have some form of Dyslexia , and although they may know and have informed
your institute, that information may not necessarily reach tutors. Statistics for ADHD suggest that
between 5% and 10% of the Australian population have some form of ADHD . Rather than using either of these in content, the paragraph plugin should be used to create
navigable, structured content; and the bold, underline, and italic plugins should be used to add
appropriate emphasis which can be picked up by a much wider range of users. One of the other features which came about from the creation of Atto was the ability for
individual users to select their own editor (rather than a single site-wide selection). This in turn
means that others can contribute other editors to Moodle if they do not like the Atto editor. In addition, we've worked to create an extensive editor framework for Atto to enable you to
create your own plugins, and we're seeing a range of community-contributed plugins beginning to appear already using that framework. You're welcome to create and contribute plugins for text size, and we have an existing plugin for font colour (with a selection of high-contrast colour options) and submit
it to the plugins database , but I suspect that it's unlikely that it would be included in the
core Moodle release. . Regarding the `Grey Plague`, this is unrelated to Atto and I won't discuss it in depth here, but
it relates to the extensibility of theming in Moodle. At present we have no mechanism to utilise
different icon colours for different themes without copying an entire set of icons to each theme
(not a small, or easy task). As a result, and to cater for the largest number of theme designs and
theme colour configurations we have been trying to choose colours which work with the greatest
number of background and foreground possibilities whilst still being accessible. Grey is the safest
option for the widest range of options. However, we are looking to allow for delivery-time colouring
of those icons to allow administrators to choose different colours for different themes. This is
partially discussed in MDL-45993 , and there's another related issue which I'm struggling to find
right now. I hope that this answers some of your questions. As ever, Moodle is an Open Source project and we
do welcome contributions from our community, be it in the form of testing, documentation, patches
for bugs, and contributions to the plugins database. If you're able to help with any of the above,
your contributions would be appreciated by the community as a whole. Best wishes, Andrew Nicols

ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for your explanation. I can appreciate some of these accessibility issues because I suffer from deteriorating sight and hearing, myself.  However, I would never want to deprive the world from the benefits of being able to "show" or "say" things, instead, I must live with my problems.  I do like to turn closed-captions on when I watch TV.  I wonder when these accessibility issues will affect artists and photographers, for example, and force them not to use colored paints or work only in greys?  Color is in the world around us, and I would not want to deprive 90% of the world from it.  I like the idea that someday, maybe in the user's profile, they will be able to switch between color and grey icons.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: No option to re-size with Atto and 2.7+
ResponsesInList.Text: My own deficiencies also cause me to speak up too.  What is happening here is making difficulties not only for me but for the average user.  This is like requiring subtitles to be always visible for all AV productions or like removing staircases and ramps only to make everyone use single passenger wheel chair elevators instead.  My readers tell me that in many cases they have to copy/paste text into a word document to change the contrast back to normal in order to read the content. It would be interesting to see if everyone had the choice to remove Font-Size and Font-Color or had the choice to bleach out icons, from the original design instead, how many actually would.  So far I have heard no viable reason why these options have been dropped or relocated to make them very challenging to bring back.  All I hear is a lot of theory. When I was into graphics, I had an image of a galaxy and needed to place a caption "You are Here" and indicate an arrow from there to a star near the center.  The problem was that in the white density of stars, a white arrow disappeared.  When in the blackness of space, a black arrow disappeared. The discovery was the use of a "Black-White" arrow, an image that had both arrows with a slight overlap, which could be used in any background.  I would have been laughed out of the company had I chosen to convert it all to shades of gray as the effectiveness of the picture would have been destroyed.  My point is that instead of removing all color from icons and ultimately making them look as if they are disabled, a better back color for the icon itself would be the answer. I have a friend that is significantly ADHD  who now spends a lot of time checking these icons to see what they do and he has to do it with every attempt to use them.  It is not just a simple matter of learning the new ones. As I asked either here or in another message, why is it that Font-Size and Font Color get eliminated while a new button is created for Emoticons and takes a high priority.  On a snarky note, why are not emoticons in gray?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: No option to re-size with Atto and 2.7+
ResponsesInList.Text: You provide some more good points, Steve. You see, I am not at all opposed to making content more accessible, but I think one needs to apply the "80/20" rule.  First, let's make sure that content works for 80% of the population, then let's work on the remaining 20%. However, as in your example of "ramps", it appears that some folks prefer that the 20% solution must be applied to everyone. Hmmm, this makes me think a little about statistics, and "expected value".  In the "worst case" scenario, let's say week have a solution worth 100 points for 80% of the population (e.g., colored icons), and 0 points for 20%.  The expected value will be (100*.8)+(0*.2), or 80 points.  If we have a 50 point solution (grey icons) for 100% of the population, the expected value is (50 * 1), or 50 points.  Do we want the "tail wagging the dog?" Well, you get the idea.  Some might debate the numbers in my example, and yes, if we could discover a 100 point solution for 100% of the population, this would have the highest expected value.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: No option to re-size with Atto and 2.7+
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Andrew, Thanks very much for taking the time to provide the logic behind Atto. --- it was intended to be a small and simple replacement with fewer options offered The concept is fine, there must certainly be a large number of people that want a simple and straightforward tool to create content with. The issue I see is that most users, be them design-aware or not, expect to find the tools that they have learned to use and that are present in other software toolbars; I sincerly cannot imagine MS removing them from their Office Suite nor Adobe from their Creative Suite. --- or lead to the creation of inaccessible content From my particular point of view, protectionist regimes do not tend to do any good to anyone. Knifes shouldn't be made because they lead to the killing of people or animals? It is unavoidable, there'll be always people creating content that goes against each and every rule of, let's not say good design, but at least an acceptable one. It's a known fact that many people copy and paste from Word, so now, if the editor doesn't provide the basic editing tools, even more people will start doing that routine, and we know what that means. --- we opted not to create plugins for text size, and for font colour *** Since screen readers do not read out things like the background colour and font size There might not be many screen readers capable of reading formats, yet, but at least ClickHear & ClickHear Mobile seem to handle variable text and highlighting color options. HAL reads font styles, though I don't know if that includes highlight color. http://www.disabled-world.com/assistivedevices/computer/screen-readers.php "Not only do screen readers differ widely from each other, but most are highly configurable." If font size were irrelevant, screen magnifiers wouldn't be available. Truth is that many programs and screen readers include them. Take for instance: http://www.aisquared.com/products Regarding background color, software is being designed to deal with that. For example: https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/chromevis-by-google/halnfobaneppemjnonmmhngbfifnafgd "Google ChromeVis is a Google Chrome extension that magnifies any selected text on a webpage. The magnified text is displayed inside of a separate lens and preserves the original page layout. Users can change both the lens text color and the lens background color ." Finally, let's not forget the reason behind the development of CSS and user style sheets . http://webdesign.about.com/od/userstylesheets/a/aa010906.htm "Adding back the underlines or making the fonts larger is a good start towards making the Web pages I visit more accessible to me." http://www.microsoft.com/enable/products/ie10/ https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/user-stylesheet/nlfpnjpcddafclelkbgijfpdanaacdcp --- Rather than using either of these in content, the paragraph plugin should be used to create navigable, structured content; and the bold, underline, and italic plugins should be used to add appropriate emphasis which can be picked up by a much wider range of users . As I expressed in my previous post, color has never been meant to be discarded because of accesibility: http://www.w3.org/TR/2008/REC-WCAG20-20081211/#visual-audio-contrast-without-color "Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information." ---One of the other features which came about from the creation of Atto was the ability for individual users to select their own editor This is definitely a great feature. --- we've worked to create an extensive editor framework for Atto to enable you to create your own plugins This totally contradicts the first statement: "it was intended to be a small and simple replacement with fewer options offered." We certainly recognize and support the effort being done in each step to bring Moodle to what it is, but given the reasons provided I'd say that maybe some reconsideration could be done regarding Atto. What is the real benefit of having Atto? Seems to me that a lot of work is being done to develop a small and simple tool only to spend a lot time and effort to develop an editor framework so people have to do more work to get the expected editing options; take for instance the following quote regarding the horizontal rule: https://moodle.org/plugins/view.php?plugin=atto_hr "I just noticed this feature was 'missing' from the new Atto editor, and was happy to find it here". This whole Atto issue also affects other plugins, like Geshi: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=240578#p1134044 Cheers!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: No option to re-size with Atto and 2.7+
ResponsesInList.Text:
```text
"
When we wrote the Atto editor, it was intended to be a small and simple replacement with fewer options offered..."  


I am curious, for what purpose?
```
 Just before Atto was written (or was public anyway) there was a big debate about TinyMCE not being suitable for mobile devices, and various other factors, such as giving users too much power so that they could create content that didn't fit with the institution style or good web design. Comparisons were made with a number of online text editors - primarily those related to posting to forums and such rather than content creation though - and I for one strongly disagreed with that premise. Misuse by a small minority should not be dealt with by removing that ability from the majority of users ( IMO ). I presume Atto was originally intended for to meet that purpose - but to me that doesn't justify setting it as the default editor and not upgrading the power tools available from a fully powered editor such as TinyMCE. It does meet the purpose of being one of two editors available (as it is) but I would have prefered to see TinyMCE4 (or another full editor) properly integrated alongside Atto to give that genuine choice, rather than just leaving the outdated TinyMCE3 as the poor second alternative. Yes I do realise that additional editors can be contributed by the community, but to me it is a core part of Moodle which should be part of the core set up and not reliant on contributed code. But it looks like that is a lost argument - HQ have decided on ATTO and whether we like it or not its what we have, so as users we either have to work with the community to develop Atto so that it does an adequate job, work with others in the community to get another editor (besides the outdated TinyMCE v3) into the plugins database, or stick with TinyMCE by making sure users know how to set it as their own editor (or even setting it as our own site default) For me, currently (and inline with comments from users who have been involved in our beta testing), when we upgrade to 2.7 next week we will set the site default editor to TinyMCE. Atto does not provide the tools I feel are needed for us (e.g. we use the Templates function of TinyMCE to provide pre-set content) - and I am prepared to deal with the fact that the occasional user can't cope with simple design guidelines and 'misuses' the available tools - but I'm also trying to develop functionality in terms of filters that can be used in Atto, as well as watching the development of Atto plugins, so that we can soon move to that as our main editor in line with HQ and core. Hopefully in time, Atto will become the editor it is intended to be - a simple, user friendly, accessible editor with the power of a wide range of plugins to provide the full range of features that people require and the ability to easily add and remove those features (possibly on a role-by-role or capability basis). And hopefully discussions like this one will help the HQ developers, and others in the community to push it along faster so that it is ready for mainstream use.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: No option to re-size with Atto and 2.7+
ResponsesInList.Text:
Not being able to change text size is very frustrating. I have a lot
of cloze questions in my courses, and I use a smaller text size for the
questions for 2 reasons. 1
- so as the person creating & editing the questions, I can easily
identify the question amongst the text. (see pic below & attached) 2
- because the drop-down menu box appeared (in 2.5) quite tall compared
with the rest of the text, I found that by reducing the font size, it
also reduced the size of the drop-down menu box and fitted in much more
nicely with the rest of the text. (I don't have a pic for this sorry, as I have already changed to 2.7 and I didn't realise there's be any change to this.) These would both be helpful for me in 2.7. As would the full-page editor. In
2.7 I also note that the new drop-down menu boxes are identical in
size. Unfortunately this is also not ideal for me, as I had some very
short answer (e.g. yes, no) drop-down menu boxes that fitted snugly into
tables in cloze questions, and now the longer box makes the layout of
my page look rather odd. Tables are an interesting challenge in
themselves and I'm not looking forward to adjusting those again. Perhaps
an option to choose whether to have the box the same size as the
longest answer or to have a certain pre-set length would be helpful. So,
for the time being, I have gone back to TinyMCE, but I'm worried that I
will be forced to stop creating questions for my course because of the
lack of functionality in my editor. I'm trying to pump as many out now before TinyMCE disappears. I
do feel frustrated, because TinyMCE wasn't ideal in a lot of ways, but I
managed to work around it and get it to work for me. I feel that Moodle
forced me to do this, even though I would have preferred to have more
advanced editing like paragraph spacing. However, I utilised font size
and tables to make my cloze questions work the way I want, and look the
way I want them too, and I was happy with that. Now,
with the changes to the editor, I feel I have to make new workarounds
and figure out new ways, or just suck it up and say well that's the way
Moodle wants me to create my questions, and there's no room for my
individuality or creativity, and it doesn't fit with the look and feel
of my existing course. This makes me sad. My
main concern/gripe is: when changing to a new version, why are there so
many things that need to be altered? I don't have any plugins for this
very reason, yet I still must manually change some things. Often things
that had to be previously altered from the last upgrade, e.g. Theme. Is that just the nature of computers? I'm no technology expert, which I think is part of the problem. However, it should be expected and accepted that not all teachers *are* technology experts.
We are education experts though, and it would be great if you could
consider that what might be 'easy' in the mind of a techie might be
illogical and confusing in the mind of a non-techie. Following
my update from 2.5 to 2.7, I had to move all my carefully crafted
blocks from the right hand side (in Orange theme) to the left hand side
(in 'More' theme, which initially I thought was a link to 'More
information' about Themes), because the Quiz navigation is on the right
hand side now, and I can't move it to the left, as it was previously in
my Quizzes. I only want one side bar, so had to move these to work with
the existing Quiz navigation block. This was time-consuming and
frustrating to say the least, as I'd had to do a similar thing when
moving to the 'Orange' theme. Then, when the Atto editor didn't have the
functionality I expected, that was the icing on the cake in my
frustration and disappointment. Maybe
I need to learn HTML to present my Cloze questions the way I want
them... but that seems (in my opinion) to defeat the usability &
accesibility of Moodle. As
for font colour and highlighting, most teachers I know are aware of
their students' capabilities and create resources that embrace different
learning styles and learning abilities. We are aware of different types
of colour-blindness and access difficulties. Please don't restrict our
creativity based on your assumptions. I
would be grateful if you could consider the above and either continue
to support TinyMCE or make changes to Atto to include font size, font
colour, highlighting, and other functions that were available in
TinyMCE. Thank you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: No option to re-size with Atto and 2.7+
ResponsesInList.Text: I suspect that after thinking about this, and the reasons given above to reduce the options available with the atto editor, most people would see that the option to do something is not the same as removing the option altogether. One is giving the user a choice, and the other is denying the user a choice. I would have to agree with the idea that abundant choice is the beginning of a new and distasteful tyranny, but the reality is that teachers, course creators, course makers, what ever you call them, are going to build a course for their users. Much of the evidence cited above is not relevant to the needs of individual classes anyway, not in many other countries where Moodle is used, and not for much longer in Oz. Like many other things, the arguments cited for containing atto sound good, but upon closer inspection, are based upon several untenable conclusions, or ignore a wider need. To suggest, for example, that the ability to resize text, change colour exists in TinyMCE, and does not need to exist for atto is based in what need? Who's need?  To suggest that " Grey is the safest option for the widest range of options. " is based in what evidence, which conclusions? Older users may need a higher degree of contrast, and for someone to suggest that the grey is the safest option is completely ignoring those needs. To make it "better", people are being urged to create plugins for atto, to add functionality. That works fine in many circumstances, but what about those who do not know how to create plugins. "OK Learn!" sounds a little like "Let them eat cake." The other side is that plugins created may not suit a large percentage of needs. Another aspect is that many admins can do anythign they like inside their Moodles but are reliant upon others, outside of their influence, to add the plugins into code. How about creating a plugin that allows the Moodle to write plugins to the right places? Not that it would compromise security in any way mind you. I rather like the idea of the atto editor, it has a number of features that I am really excited about using, but I suggest it needs a lot more thought than it is currently receiving.

ResponsesInList.Title: 2.8 Auto-Save with no Full Screen--Unfortunate. Re: No option to re-size with Atto and 2.7+
ResponsesInList.Text: Title says it all, but a testimonial of how the Atto decisions are creating problems for my promotion of Moodle as our new LMS might help. I'm presenting Moodle to full faculty next week, after piloting with a small cohort and 200 students. We used TinyMCE for our first user test, in 2.7.2. Teachers reacted to the online text submission view by saying: "It feels like writing an email." " Not to worry ," I said. "Just click the Full Screen button and it feels like writing on Google Docs ." "Ooh," they said. "And watch this," I said, and toggled the "More tools" button. More oohs. "Actually a better user experience than Google Docs, that toolbar ," I said. They nodded agreement. *  *  * After our 200 students wrote their online essays in Assignment, the big complaint was: " Some lost their work. Google Docs auto-saves. It's better. " "Not to fear," I said. " 2.8 has auto-save, coming soon ." *  *  * So now , when I show them auto-save in 2.8 Atto-- without full-screen-- they're going to say, " It feels like writing an email. Google Docs is better. " I'm so excited about 2.8. I so appreciate the work done on it. And I so hope I don't have to wait for somebody to create a full-screen plugin. I teach, I don't code. But I do contribute to the community, and I do praise Moodle for all its goodness to all comers. On this one, though, I'm mystified by the rationale for denying choice of core Atto defaults. I truly hope this is re-considered, and soon. (Along with putting "Draft saved" popup anywhere but lower left of editor.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Editor should not pollute HTML with inline style tags
ResponsesInList.Text: I appreciate the somehow minimalistic approach by Atto with respect of formatting. But I feel it is not implemented properly. If you do copy/paste within Atto, the styling is pasted to the underlying HTML. In other words copy & paste pollutes the HTML with style attributes. why is "Heading large" a <h3> and not a <h1>. This leads to pretty strange effects in wiki numbering There is "clear formatting" - but it removes what ever, at least it does not remove all style attributes Any helpful hint is welcome.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Editor should not pollute HTML with inline style tags
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Bernhard, Atto relies on the browser implementation for much of its low level functionality. This does not always work as well as hoped.  The clear formatting button passes through to a browser command that removes styles as defined by the browser vendor. It would be possible add a method to clean styles further, but I don't think that the expected behavior would be to remove all styles, but instead only those introduced by the editor buttons. The copy/paste actions are also done completely by the browser rather than with code in Atto.  As far as I know Firefox and IE do not create the excess styles.  This is a problem specific to Chrome/Safari browsers. It would be a very complicated feature to override. I believe h3 is used because h1 and h2 are reserved for page headings in Moodle so that it is assumed that h3 would be the largest heading to appear in user content.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Editor should not pollute HTML with inline style tags
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Daniel, thanks for the reply. I tried with Firefox and indeed with Firefox we do not get the style-attributes. It does not comfort much that we have back such browser dependencies. I furtheron tried with TinyMce which does not have this effect also in Crome. I think the headline concept (h1 .. h6) in HTML is broken by design and cannot be repaired. But If the user has the choice to switch between Atto and TinyMce, the editors should behave the same with respect to the produced results. And in particular in the Wiki, <h> provides chapter wise "edit" links. So I also think it is a mistake to limit Atto to produce only h3 onwards. I also would like to provide an editor which supports the user to produce semantical markup using headers bullet and numberd list definition lists tables paragraph preformatted blockquote inlines (emphasis and strong emphasis) If we want to add further semantics I would like to do this with css classes and not with embedded styles. Therefore "clean formatting" should remove all non semantic formatting, but not those introduced by editor buttons. I saw that TinyMce also has a button "clean sourcecode" which also does something. We are currently in the process of setting the Moold strategy in our institution. After all these experiences with Atto, i tend to go back using tinyMce as default editor - but I am not sure how long it will be available. What would you advise? Bernhard

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Editor should not pollute HTML with inline style tags
ResponsesInList.Text: I find that for most things that a student would do Atto works well. The loading speed is better with Atto and if you are using Moodle 2.8 the autosave function makes it a better editor for the novice. ResponsesInList.Text: Daniel, the whole Atto plugin was using wrong approach ... and you could fix it The problem is that modern editors should never output tags - they were deprecated already in HTML4 and are not supported in HTML5 ( http://www.w3schools.com/tags/tag_font.asp ). Font tags were used in old HTMLArea editor and TinyMCE 2 long time ago but TinyMCE 3.0 has using span tags instead of font tags. Because TinyMCE has http://www.tinymce.com/wiki.php/Configuration3x:convert_fonts_to_spans enabled by default it outputs tags like testing that work fine and are not stripped by Atto.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: WANTED: A font-size option in Atto that works.
ResponsesInList.Text: Daniel, attached the debug file to show how to change the plugin. The "evil" command in original plugin is in _changeStyle: function(e, size) { document.execCommand("fontSize", false, size); } that creates font tags. It can be simply changed to _changeStyle: function(e, size) { document.execCommand("insertHTML", false, ''+document.getSelection()+''); } The original plugin has 7 values/names for font-sizes X-Small...XXX-Large and in previous insertHTML command variable size needs to give callbackArgs: size.name (not value) A more advanced font-size plugin could handle other values as well http://www.w3schools.com/cssref/pr_font_font-size.asp
